text:
ashley: quick follow-up to the tracing/cost RFC — we need to pick where inference cost tags get attached for attribution: at the edge (collector) or at runtime (inference service). short poll: edge vs runtime? :thinking:

marta: edge wins for attribution accuracy imo. if we attach before sampling we avoid losing cost signal when traces are dropped. also easier to do tenant resolution close to request.

devon: +1 on accuracy, but runtime can emit model/token-level granularity (quantized vs full, batch sizes). runtime is the only place that really knows per-call token_count reliably without bookkeeping.

oliver: tradeoffs:
- edge: cheaper, early attach, survives sampling, but may be stale/approx if we guess tokens.
- runtime: precise, includes batching breakdown, but if we sample at edge we lose the samples and the cost info for dropped traces.

ashley: agreed. idea: attach a lightweight cost-key at edge (opaque id) and resolve full cost at runtime and emit a secondary enrichment event that backfills cost fields into the trace envelope. that way attribution survives sampling but we still get runtime precision when available.

marta: sounds promising. how would backfill work with our ingestion pipeline? if enrichment events arrive later than trace window we could lose joinability.

devon: we could use a 24h join window metadata store (small write) keyed by cost-key. runtime writes: {cost_key -> {model, tokens, quantization, batch_size}}. ingest pipeline can late-join when search indexes are queried or during post-process billing jobs.

ashley: example header we propose adding at edge:
```
X-Cost-Key: ck_01F3a9bX
X-Tenant-ID: acme
```
runtime would write a backfill record:
```
PUT /cost-ledger/ck_01F3a9bX -> {model: "gpt-4o", tokens: 120, quant: "q4_0", batch: 8}
```

oliver: concerns: 1) we introduce another storage surface to maintain -> needs TTL/GC 2) query performance for billing joins 3) potential privacy if cost-meta contains model names (should we hash?).

marta: on (1) TTL ok, we should align with retention policy and auto-expire 48h by default. on (3) prefer storing model_id not full descriptive name; billing jobs can map id->meta in a controlled job.

devon: sampling policy change: if we keep attaching cost-key at edge we should NOT sample away the entire envelope for quota-sensitive customers — otherwise metrics will be skewed. maybe keep a tiny sampled header for cost-only traces (small payload).

ashley: implementation checklist I can take:
- add X-Cost-Key generation to edge proxy (implemented as short opaque uuid)
- add runtime writer to cost-ledger with TTL (48h)
- add pipeline join step for late enrichment in the billing job and for query-time joins
- doc + rollout plan + feature flag

marta: add me for tests: I'll own query-side validation and SLO impact tests.

oliver: infra-bot FYI: this will add ~1.2k writes/s at p95 traffic if we keep cost-ledger writes synchronous. can we batch writes from runtime?

infra-bot: estimated impact: 1.2k writes/s -> ~100k/day. recommend batched writes to Dynamo-style store or cached write-behind to reduce RPS. suggest using 1s micro-batches.

devon: for accuracy we need the runtime to write immediately or within 1-2s. batched 1s is fine. we also need once-only semantics (idempotency) - use conditional put with ttl.

ashley: rollout plan:
1) feature flag on edge to emit X-Cost-Key (no ledger writes) - collect telemetry on missing backfills
2) enable runtime backfill writer in a canary fleet + write-behind batching
3) enable pipeline join in billing job, run backfill reconciliation job for 7 days
4) flip flag globally

marta: test plan: synthetic load test for 100k/day, join coverage tests, regression check for query latency on billing reports.

oliver: doc note: call the feature `cost-key-handshake` in the console so sales/entitlement teams can opt-out for regulated customers.

ashley: one more question: do we need to propagate cost-key to downstream services (plugins, toolcallers) that might add tokens? probably yes — runtime should merge token counts from third-party tool calls.

devon: runtime will aggregate tool tokens into the same cost record. we need a deterministic merge strategy: add to tokens field and add subentries for tool breakdown if present.

marta: ack. can we keep the initial RFC doc updated with this handshake pattern and the small diagram? I'll make a short appendix.

ashley: sounds good. action items assigned. i'll create the PR for edge header + runtime writer tomorrow. tagging @marta @devon @oliver for visibility. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-bot: new PR detected -> redwood/edge-proxy#842 will run integration tests when CI returns.

ashley: thanks — will follow up with the PR link in this thread when ready.
